Civix — Discord Bot + CAD
Features Communities Customize CAD Setup Log in
Multi-community · Each community isolated & secure

Meet Civix — one bot, every community its own world.

Civix now runs per community: anyone can register a community and gets its own settings, currency, departments, ranks, jobs and CAD records — completely separate from every other community. Nothing is forced to SDRP's setup. Row Level Security locks each community's data to its members, and the bot picks up settings changes automatically. The site and CAD run free on Cloudflare Pages + Supabase, while the bot runs on Node.js from your own machine.

Create your account

The CAD data lives in the cloud, so the dashboard stays online around the clock — even when the laptop running Civix is off.

Your stack — $0/month

Exactly the setup you picked — no card required. One free-tier catch: Supabase pauses after about a week of inactivity (you just unpause it in the dashboard). Cloudflare Pages itself never sleeps.

Communities

Every community gets its own Civix

Create a community and Civix creates a completely separate space for it — its own bot settings, its own CAD, its own members and roles. Switching communities switches everything you see in the CAD and Customize dashboards. No community inherits another community's departments, ranks, jobs or currency.

Create your community

You become the owner. A blank configuration is created for you — add your own currency name, departments, ranks and jobs from Customize. Nothing is pre-filled with SDRP's or anyone else's setup.

In demo mode the community is created in this tab only. With Supabase connected, this calls the create_community database function (Setup step 1), which creates the community, your owner row in community_members, and an empty bot_settings row in a single call. It is the only way to create a community: there is deliberately no direct INSERT policy on communities, so the database denies direct inserts outright — and the membership policy requires an owner/admin who doesn't exist yet on a new community.

Your communities

How isolation & security work

community_id on everything: every CAD table (units, citizens, vehicles, citations, BOLOs) and bot_settings carries a community_id. Queries always filter by the active community.

Row Level Security from day one: RLS is enabled in the setup SQL — nobody can touch another community's rows, owners/admins manage settings, and CAD access is split into view / create / edit / delete rights that each community grants per access role (Customize → CAD permissions), so being a member no longer means being able to modify records. The bot uses the service role on your laptop only.

The owner is protected: admins can manage officer, dispatch and civilian memberships, but the membership policies block them from modifying, demoting or deleting the actual owner's row — and from granting the owner role to anyone, including themselves. Guard triggers go further: the owner's own row can't be deleted or demoted even by the owner (no accidental lockout), and communities.owner_id can only be changed by the current owner, so ownership can't be taken by editing the community row. Communities themselves can only be created through the create_community function — there is no direct insert policy on the communities table.

Access roles ≠ your structure: the roles in community_members (owner / admin / officer / dispatch / civilian) are system access levels only — they decide who can do what. They are not your departments, ranks or job titles: those are free-form lists each community writes itself in Customize, and they never gate database access.

Profiles auto-created: a database trigger on auth.users creates the profiles row the moment someone signs up — no manual step.

Customize Civix

Customize everything about the bot — for the selected community

Pick a community at the top of the dashboard first — every change saves to that community only. Set its name, prefix and status, its own currency and economy numbers, every panel, its own jobs, departments and ranks, protection and moderation rules, ticket settings, messages and embed look — plus an on/off switch for every feature, and per-role CAD permissions deciding who can view, create, edit and delete records. New communities start from a genuinely blank config: no currency name, balances, departments, ranks or channels are pre-filled. With Supabase connected, saving pushes the change live to the bot via Realtime, no restart or manual reload.

How to connect it ↓

Accounts

Log in / sign up

Accounts are handled by Supabase Auth — sign-up, login, sessions and password resets are built in, so there's no auth code for you to write or secure yourself.

just looking around?

Demo preview runs entirely in this tab — nothing you type or add is saved anywhere. Real accounts work as soon as you paste your Supabase keys in (Setup, step 2).

  • ✓Email + password accounts out of the box, with confirmation emails and password reset handled by Supabase.
  • ✓Link Discord later: Supabase Auth also supports "Sign in with Discord" (OAuth) — turn it on in the Supabase dashboard when you want members to log in with the same account they use in your server.
  • ✓Profile created automatically: the setup SQL includes a trigger (on_auth_user_created) that inserts a profiles row the instant Supabase Auth creates a user — display name comes from signup, default role is civilian.
  • ✓Community roles are separate: global profile holds who you are; community_members holds your role inside each community (owner / admin / officer / dispatch / civilian). You can be an officer in one community and a civilian in another.
  • ✓Your bot uses the same login system: the bot never handles passwords — it reads profiles + community_members to know who's an officer in that community.

How login flows

Member signs up here → Supabase Auth creates the account → the trigger creates their profiles row → they create or join a community → a community_members row gives them a role in that community → CAD, Customize and the bot all enforce that role via Row Level Security.

Setup guide

Go live on Cloudflare — 5 steps (multi-community + secure)

This page is the whole website. Follow these steps and it's live on Cloudflare Pages with working logins, per-community CAD and settings, Row Level Security enabled from the start, and a bot that receives settings automatically. Total cost: $0.

1

Create the Supabase project — multi-community schema, RLS & profile trigger

Sign up at supabase.com → New project (free). Open the SQL Editor, paste this, and run it. It creates communities, membership, per-community CAD tables and per-community bot_settings, enables Row Level Security with real policies (not postponed), and adds the trigger that auto-creates a profile on signup. Run this before storing any real community data. The script is safe to rerun — existing policies are dropped before being recreated and the Realtime step checks before adding bot_settings — so if a run stops partway, just run it again. If you ran the old single-community SQL, drop those old tables first — the shape is different.

-- ===== Civix multi-community setup — safe to run more than once =====
-- Every policy is dropped (if it exists) before it is recreated, the
-- triggers and functions use create-or-replace, and the Realtime step
-- at the end checks whether bot_settings is already in the
-- publication before adding it — so rerunning this script after a
-- partial or earlier run won't fail on "already exists" errors.

-- ===== Communities =====
create table if not exists communities (
  id uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),
  name text not null,
  guild_id text unique,
  description text,
  owner_id uuid not null references auth.users on delete cascade,
  created_at timestamptz default now()
);

create table if not exists profiles (
  id uuid primary key references auth.users on delete cascade,
  display_name text,
  created_at timestamptz default now()
);

create table if not exists community_members (
  community_id uuid not null references communities on delete cascade,
  user_id uuid not null references auth.users on delete cascade,
  role text not null default 'civilian'
    check (role in ('owner','admin','officer','dispatch','civilian')),
  created_at timestamptz default now(),
  primary key (community_id, user_id)
);

-- Auto-create profile on signup (was missing before)
create or replace function public.handle_new_user()
returns trigger language plpgsql security definer set search_path = public as $$
begin
  insert into public.profiles (id, display_name)
  values (new.id, coalesce(new.raw_user_meta_data->>'display_name',''))
  on conflict (id) do nothing;
  return new;
end; $$;
drop trigger if exists on_auth_user_created on auth.users;
create trigger on_auth_user_created
  after insert on auth.users
  for each row execute function public.handle_new_user();

-- Helpers for RLS (security definer avoids recursive policies)
create or replace function public.is_member(cid uuid)
returns boolean language sql security definer set search_path = public stable as $$
  select exists(select 1 from community_members where community_id = cid and user_id = auth.uid());
$$;
create or replace function public.is_community_admin(cid uuid)
returns boolean language sql security definer set search_path = public stable as $$
  select exists(select 1 from community_members where community_id = cid and user_id = auth.uid() and role in ('owner','admin'));
$$;
create or replace function public.is_community_owner(cid uuid)
returns boolean language sql security definer set search_path = public stable as $$
  select exists(select 1 from community_members where community_id = cid and user_id = auth.uid() and role = 'owner');
$$;
-- The community's actual owner, from communities.owner_id — the one
-- membership row an admin must never be able to touch.
create or replace function public.community_owner_id(cid uuid)
returns uuid language sql security definer set search_path = public stable as $$
  select owner_id from communities where id = cid;
$$;

-- ===== Per-community CAD + settings (community_id on EVERYTHING) =====
create table if not exists citizens (
  id bigint generated always as identity primary key,
  community_id uuid not null references communities on delete cascade,
  full_name text not null, dob date, address text,
  warrants boolean default false, notes text,
  created_at timestamptz default now()
);
create table if not exists vehicles (
  id bigint generated always as identity primary key,
  community_id uuid not null references communities on delete cascade,
  plate text not null, owner_name text, model text, color text,
  stolen boolean default false, created_at timestamptz default now(),
  unique (community_id, plate)
);
create table if not exists citations (
  id bigint generated always as identity primary key,
  community_id uuid not null references communities on delete cascade,
  citizen_name text not null, officer text, violation text not null,
  fine int default 0, status text default 'unpaid',
  created_at timestamptz default now()
);
create table if not exists bolos (
  id bigint generated always as identity primary key,
  community_id uuid not null references communities on delete cascade,
  subject text not null, details text, active boolean default true,
  created_at timestamptz default now()
);
create table if not exists units (
  id bigint generated always as identity primary key,
  community_id uuid not null references communities on delete cascade,
  callsign text not null, officer text, status text default '10-8',
  updated_at timestamptz default now(),
  unique (community_id, callsign)
);
-- One settings row PER community (replaces the old single 'main' row)
create table if not exists bot_settings (
  community_id uuid primary key references communities on delete cascade,
  config jsonb not null default '{}'::jsonb,
  updated_at timestamptz default now()
);

-- ===== Row Level Security — enabled from the start =====
alter table communities enable row level security;
alter table profiles enable row level security;
alter table community_members enable row level security;
alter table citizens enable row level security;
alter table vehicles enable row level security;
alter table citations enable row level security;
alter table bolos enable row level security;
alter table units enable row level security;
alter table bot_settings enable row level security;

drop policy if exists "profiles: own row" on profiles;
create policy "profiles: own row" on profiles for all
  using (id = auth.uid()) with check (id = auth.uid());
drop policy if exists "communities: members read" on communities;
create policy "communities: members read" on communities for select
  using (owner_id = auth.uid() or public.is_member(id));
-- NO insert policy on communities — on purpose. With RLS enabled and
-- no INSERT policy, Postgres denies every direct insert into
-- communities, for every user. The create_community() SECURITY DEFINER
-- function further down is the ONLY way to create a community: it runs
-- as the database owner (bypassing RLS internally), so it works even
-- though no insert policy exists. If you ran an earlier version of
-- this SQL, this drop removes the old direct-insert policy:
drop policy if exists "communities: create own" on communities;
drop policy if exists "communities: owner/admin update" on communities;
create policy "communities: owner/admin update" on communities for update
  using (public.is_community_admin(id))
  with check (public.is_community_admin(id));
drop policy if exists "members: see own communities" on community_members;
create policy "members: see own communities" on community_members for select
  using (user_id = auth.uid() or public.is_member(community_id));

-- ===== Membership management — the owner is protected =====
-- The old single "owner/admin manage" policy (dropped just below) let
-- ANY owner/admin change ANY membership row — an admin could demote
-- or delete the actual owner, or promote themselves to owner. It is
-- replaced by one policy per action, and every one of them applies
-- the same two owner guards on top of is_community_admin():
--   1. Owner-level rows are owner-only: a row whose role is 'owner'
--      can only be created, changed or deleted by someone who is
--      themselves an owner (is_community_owner). In the UPDATE/DELETE
--      policies the USING clause looks at the EXISTING row, so an
--      admin cannot even target the owner's row; in the WITH CHECK
--      clauses the NEW row is checked, so an admin cannot promote
--      themselves (or anyone) to 'owner' either.
--   2. The actual owner's row is untouchable by anyone else: a row
--      whose user_id is the community's owner_id (communities table)
--      can only be modified by that owner — checked against both the
--      existing row (USING) and the new row (WITH CHECK), so an admin
--      can't reassign, demote or delete it, and can't insert a
--      replacement row for the owner either.
-- Admins keep full control over NON-owner memberships (admin /
-- officer / dispatch / civilian) — day-to-day member management is
-- unchanged. The triggers after these policies add the final guard:
-- the owner cannot accidentally lock themselves out.
drop policy if exists "members: owner/admin manage" on community_members;
drop policy if exists "members: add members" on community_members;
drop policy if exists "members: update members" on community_members;
drop policy if exists "members: remove members" on community_members;
drop policy if exists "members: add members" on community_members;
create policy "members: add members" on community_members for insert
  with check (
    public.is_community_admin(community_id)
    and (role != 'owner' or public.is_community_owner(community_id))
    and (user_id != public.community_owner_id(community_id)
         or auth.uid() = public.community_owner_id(community_id))
  );
drop policy if exists "members: update members" on community_members;
create policy "members: update members" on community_members for update
  using (
    public.is_community_admin(community_id)
    and (role != 'owner' or public.is_community_owner(community_id))
    and (user_id != public.community_owner_id(community_id)
         or auth.uid() = public.community_owner_id(community_id))
  )
  with check (
    public.is_community_admin(community_id)
    and (role != 'owner' or public.is_community_owner(community_id))
    and (user_id != public.community_owner_id(community_id)
         or auth.uid() = public.community_owner_id(community_id))
  );
drop policy if exists "members: remove members" on community_members;
create policy "members: remove members" on community_members for delete
  using (
    public.is_community_admin(community_id)
    and (role != 'owner' or public.is_community_owner(community_id))
    and (user_id != public.community_owner_id(community_id)
         or auth.uid() = public.community_owner_id(community_id))
  );

-- Lockout & takeover guards (triggers — they fire even where a
-- policy can't see the old row, and they also stop the service_role
-- bot key from making these changes by accident):
--  * The actual owner's membership row can never be deleted, demoted,
--    moved to another community or reassigned to another user — not
--    even by the owner themselves, so an owner can never accidentally
--    leave their own community ownerless or lock themselves out.
--  * The last remaining 'owner' row of a community gets the same
--    protection if it isn't the actual owner's row.
--  * Granting 'owner' to anyone requires already being an owner.
--  * communities.owner_id can only be changed by the current owner —
--    an admin who can edit the community row still cannot rewrite
--    owner_id to themselves and take the community over that way.
create or replace function public.protect_owner_membership()
returns trigger language plpgsql security definer set search_path = public as $$
declare
  v_actual uuid := public.community_owner_id(old.community_id);
  v_owners int;
begin
  if tg_op = 'DELETE' then
    -- Community itself is being deleted (cascade) — nothing to protect.
    if not exists(select 1 from public.communities where id = old.community_id) then
      return old;
    end if;
    if old.user_id = v_actual then
      raise exception 'The community owner''s membership cannot be deleted — the community would be left without its owner';
    end if;
    if old.role = 'owner' then
      select count(*) into v_owners from public.community_members
        where community_id = old.community_id and role = 'owner';
      if v_owners = 1 then
        raise exception 'Cannot delete the last owner of a community';
      end if;
    end if;
    return old;
  end if;
  -- UPDATE
  if old.user_id = v_actual
     and (new.role != 'owner' or new.user_id != old.user_id
          or new.community_id != old.community_id) then
    raise exception 'The community owner''s membership cannot be demoted, moved or reassigned';
  end if;
  if new.role = 'owner' and old.role != 'owner'
     and not public.is_community_owner(old.community_id) then
    raise exception 'Only the community owner can grant the owner role';
  end if;
  if old.role = 'owner' and new.role != 'owner' then
    select count(*) into v_owners from public.community_members
      where community_id = old.community_id and role = 'owner';
    if v_owners = 1 then
      raise exception 'Cannot demote the last owner of a community';
    end if;
  end if;
  return new;
end; $$;
drop trigger if exists protect_owner_membership on community_members;
create trigger protect_owner_membership
  before update or delete on community_members
  for each row execute function public.protect_owner_membership();

create or replace function public.protect_community_ownership()
returns trigger language plpgsql security definer set search_path = public as $$
begin
  if new.owner_id != old.owner_id and auth.uid() is distinct from old.owner_id then
    raise exception 'Only the current owner can transfer ownership of a community';
  end if;
  return new;
end; $$;
drop trigger if exists protect_community_ownership on communities;
create trigger protect_community_ownership
  before update on communities
  for each row execute function public.protect_community_ownership();

-- ===== CAD permissions — per community, per access role, per action =====
-- Being a member is NOT enough to modify CAD records. Each community
-- decides, for each access role, who may view / create / edit / delete
-- CAD records. The grants live in that community's own config:
--   bot_settings.config -> 'permissions' -> 'cad' -> <role> -> {view,create,edit,delete}
-- edited in Customize → CAD permissions. Until a community grants a
-- right, it is denied (secure by default). Owners always have full
-- access and can't be locked out of their own CAD.
-- NOTE: the roles here (owner/admin/officer/dispatch/civilian) are
-- SYSTEM access levels from community_members — they only gate access.
-- A community's own departments, ranks and job titles are free-form
-- lists inside its config and never appear in these policies.
create or replace function public.cad_allowed(cid uuid, action text)
returns boolean language plpgsql security definer set search_path = public stable as $$
declare
  v_role text;
  v_cfg jsonb;
begin
  select role into v_role from public.community_members
    where community_id = cid and user_id = auth.uid();
  if v_role is null then return false; end if;
  if v_role = 'owner' then return true; end if;
  select config into v_cfg from public.bot_settings where community_id = cid;
  return coalesce((v_cfg #>> array['permissions','cad',v_role,action]) = 'true', false);
end; $$;

-- One policy per action, per CAD table — no more "any member can edit"
drop policy if exists "citizens: view" on citizens;
create policy "citizens: view" on citizens for select
  using (public.cad_allowed(community_id, 'view'));
drop policy if exists "citizens: create" on citizens;
create policy "citizens: create" on citizens for insert
  with check (public.cad_allowed(community_id, 'create'));
drop policy if exists "citizens: edit" on citizens;
create policy "citizens: edit" on citizens for update
  using (public.cad_allowed(community_id, 'edit'))
  with check (public.cad_allowed(community_id, 'edit'));
drop policy if exists "citizens: delete" on citizens;
create policy "citizens: delete" on citizens for delete
  using (public.cad_allowed(community_id, 'delete'));
drop policy if exists "vehicles: view" on vehicles;
create policy "vehicles: view" on vehicles for select
  using (public.cad_allowed(community_id, 'view'));
drop policy if exists "vehicles: create" on vehicles;
create policy "vehicles: create" on vehicles for insert
  with check (public.cad_allowed(community_id, 'create'));
drop policy if exists "vehicles: edit" on vehicles;
create policy "vehicles: edit" on vehicles for update
  using (public.cad_allowed(community_id, 'edit'))
  with check (public.cad_allowed(community_id, 'edit'));
drop policy if exists "vehicles: delete" on vehicles;
create policy "vehicles: delete" on vehicles for delete
  using (public.cad_allowed(community_id, 'delete'));
drop policy if exists "citations: view" on citations;
create policy "citations: view" on citations for select
  using (public.cad_allowed(community_id, 'view'));
drop policy if exists "citations: create" on citations;
create policy "citations: create" on citations for insert
  with check (public.cad_allowed(community_id, 'create'));
drop policy if exists "citations: edit" on citations;
create policy "citations: edit" on citations for update
  using (public.cad_allowed(community_id, 'edit'))
  with check (public.cad_allowed(community_id, 'edit'));
drop policy if exists "citations: delete" on citations;
create policy "citations: delete" on citations for delete
  using (public.cad_allowed(community_id, 'delete'));
drop policy if exists "bolos: view" on bolos;
create policy "bolos: view" on bolos for select
  using (public.cad_allowed(community_id, 'view'));
drop policy if exists "bolos: create" on bolos;
create policy "bolos: create" on bolos for insert
  with check (public.cad_allowed(community_id, 'create'));
drop policy if exists "bolos: edit" on bolos;
create policy "bolos: edit" on bolos for update
  using (public.cad_allowed(community_id, 'edit'))
  with check (public.cad_allowed(community_id, 'edit'));
drop policy if exists "bolos: delete" on bolos;
create policy "bolos: delete" on bolos for delete
  using (public.cad_allowed(community_id, 'delete'));
drop policy if exists "units: view" on units;
create policy "units: view" on units for select
  using (public.cad_allowed(community_id, 'view'));
drop policy if exists "units: create" on units;
create policy "units: create" on units for insert
  with check (public.cad_allowed(community_id, 'create'));
drop policy if exists "units: edit" on units;
create policy "units: edit" on units for update
  using (public.cad_allowed(community_id, 'edit'))
  with check (public.cad_allowed(community_id, 'edit'));
drop policy if exists "units: delete" on units;
create policy "units: delete" on units for delete
  using (public.cad_allowed(community_id, 'delete'));
drop policy if exists "settings: members read" on bot_settings;
create policy "settings: members read" on bot_settings for select
  using (public.is_member(community_id));
drop policy if exists "settings: admins write" on bot_settings;
create policy "settings: admins write" on bot_settings for all
  using (public.is_community_admin(community_id))
  with check (public.is_community_admin(community_id));

-- ===== Community creation — RPC only, no direct inserts =====
-- There is deliberately NO insert policy on communities (see above),
-- so a direct insert into communities is denied for everyone — this
-- function is the only supported way to create one. It is needed for
-- a second reason too: the membership insert policy only lets an
-- existing owner/admin add a member, and the bot_settings write
-- policy requires the same. A brand-new community has NO members yet,
-- so the creator can never insert their own owner row directly — and
-- without that row, the bot_settings insert is blocked too. That
-- deadlock is fixed here, not by loosening the policies: this
-- SECURITY DEFINER function runs as the database owner (bypassing
-- RLS internally) and creates all three rows atomically in one call.
-- It only ever acts for the signed-in caller (auth.uid()) and only
-- ever makes THAT caller the owner, so RLS stays fully enforced
-- everywhere else — no one can use it to join or claim someone
-- else's community.
create or replace function public.create_community(
  p_name text,
  p_guild_id text default null,
  p_description text default null
)
returns uuid language plpgsql security definer set search_path = public as $$
declare
  v_uid uuid := auth.uid();
  v_id uuid;
begin
  if v_uid is null then
    raise exception 'You must be signed in to create a community';
  end if;
  if p_name is null or btrim(p_name) = '' then
    raise exception 'Community name is required';
  end if;
  insert into public.communities (name, guild_id, description, owner_id)
  values (
    btrim(p_name),
    nullif(btrim(coalesce(p_guild_id, '')), ''),
    nullif(btrim(coalesce(p_description, '')), ''),
    v_uid
  )
  returning id into v_id;
  -- Creator's owner membership — the row direct inserts can't create
  insert into public.community_members (community_id, user_id, role)
  values (v_id, v_uid, 'owner');
  -- Blank per-community settings row — the community customizes from
  -- scratch on first Save in Customize; nothing is pre-filled.
  insert into public.bot_settings (community_id, config)
  values (v_id, '{}'::jsonb);
  return v_id;
end; $$;
revoke all on function public.create_community(text, text, text) from public;
grant execute on function public.create_community(text, text, text) to authenticated;

-- ===== Owner protection — verification checklist =====
-- Work through these with two test accounts (owner + admin) after
-- running this SQL; every line is the expected result:
--  1. Admin updates or deletes the owner's community_members row
--     -> blocked: the UPDATE/DELETE policies' USING clauses exclude
--        owner rows and the actual owner's row for non-owners.
--  2. Admin updates their OWN row to role 'owner' (self-promotion)
--     -> blocked: WITH CHECK rejects a new 'owner' row from anyone
--        who is not already an owner, and the protect_owner_
--        membership trigger raises as a second line of defence.
--  3. Admin inserts a new membership row with role 'owner'
--     -> blocked by the INSERT policy's owner guard.
--  4. Admin updates communities.owner_id to their own user id
--     -> blocked: the protect_community_ownership trigger only lets
--        the current owner change owner_id (ownership transfer).
--  5. Owner deletes or demotes their OWN membership row
--     -> blocked by the protect_owner_membership trigger: the
--        actual owner's row can't be deleted, demoted, moved or
--        reassigned, so an owner can't accidentally lock themselves
--        (or the community) out. Same for the last 'owner' row.
--  6. Any signed-in user inserts directly into communities
--     -> denied: RLS is on and there is no INSERT policy at all —
--        sb.rpc('create_community', …) is the only creation path.
--  7. Admin manages officer / dispatch / civilian memberships
--     -> still works exactly as before — only owner-level rows
--        and the actual owner's row are restricted.

-- Realtime so the bot receives settings automatically.
-- Guarded so the script is safe to rerun: adding a table that is
-- already in the publication would error, so check first.
do $$
begin
  if not exists (
    select 1 from pg_publication_tables
    where pubname = 'supabase_realtime'
      and schemaname = 'public'
      and tablename = 'bot_settings'
  ) then
    alter publication supabase_realtime add table public.bot_settings;
  end if;
end $$;

Security notes: the anon key in the web page can only do what RLS allows for the signed-in user — it cannot read another community's rows. The service_role key bypasses RLS, so it stays only in your laptop bot, never in this page. Creating a community must go through the create_community function above — and now it is the only way that works. There is no INSERT policy on communities at all, so with RLS on, every direct insert is denied; the function is SECURITY DEFINER, so it creates the community, the creator's owner membership row, and the blank bot_settings row in one atomic call (which also sidesteps the chicken-and-egg problem: the membership policy requires an existing owner/admin, who doesn't exist yet on a new community) — while every other table keeps enforcing RLS exactly as written. The site calls it with sb.rpc('create_community', …); nothing else in the app creates communities, memberships for new communities, or first settings rows by inserting directly. Owner protection: membership management is split into separate add / update / remove policies, and all three carry the same owner guards — an admin can manage officer, dispatch and civilian memberships as before, but cannot target a row whose role is owner, cannot touch the actual owner's row (the one whose user_id is the community's owner_id), and cannot create an owner row, including promoting themselves. Two triggers back the policies up: protect_owner_membership makes the actual owner's row impossible to delete, demote, move or reassign — even by the owner — so an owner can't accidentally lock themselves out or leave the community ownerless, and protect_community_ownership means communities.owner_id can only be changed by the current owner, so an admin can't take ownership by editing the community row either. A scenario-by-scenario verification checklist is included as comments at the end of the SQL above. CAD permissions: CAD tables no longer use member-only policies — each action (view / create / edit / delete) checks cad_allowed(), which reads the caller's access role and the grants stored in that community's config (permissions.cad). Nothing is granted until the community's owner sets it in Customize → CAD permissions, and owners always keep full access.

2

Paste your Supabase keys into this page

In Supabase: Project Settings → API. Copy the Project URL and the anon public key, and paste them into the two constants at the top of the script in index.html. The login form, Communities, CAD and Customize switch from demo mode to live data automatically. The anon key is safe to ship because RLS from Step 1 is on — without RLS it would not be safe. Never put the service_role key in this page; that one belongs only in your bot.

const SUPABASE_URL = "https://YOUR-PROJECT.supabase.co";
const SUPABASE_ANON_KEY = "YOUR-ANON-PUBLIC-KEY";
3

Deploy to Cloudflare Pages

Push this file to a GitHub repo, then in Cloudflare: Workers & Pages → Create → Pages → Connect to Git → pick the repo. Framework preset: None. Build command: leave empty. Output directory: /. Deploy — you'll get a free *.pages.dev address, and you can attach your own domain in the Pages project under Custom domains whenever you buy one. Every future edit is just a git push.

4

Connect your Node.js bot

Your bot stays on your laptop. Install the Supabase client in your bot project and use the service_role key there (it never leaves your machine — it bypasses RLS, so it must never go in a web page). Every query must be scoped to a community: resolve the Discord guild to its community first, then filter by community_id on every read/write.

npm install @supabase/supabase-js

// bot.js — add near your other requires
const { createClient } = require('@supabase/supabase-js');
const supabase = createClient(
  process.env.SUPABASE_URL,
  process.env.SUPABASE_SERVICE_KEY  // service_role key, laptop only
);

// Resolve this Discord server to its Civix community
async function communityForGuild(guildId) {
  const { data } = await supabase
    .from('communities').select('id, name')
    .eq('guild_id', guildId).single();
  return data; // null = this guild has no community yet
}

// Example: /cad search by plate — inside ONE community only
const community = await communityForGuild(interaction.guildId);
const { data } = await supabase
  .from('vehicles')
  .select('*')
  .eq('community_id', community.id)
  .eq('plate', plate.toUpperCase())
  .single();
5

The bot implementation — settings loaded & applied per community

This is the actual settings module for the bot, not just a subscription snippet. Drop it in as settings.js: on startup it loads every community's own row from bot_settings into a cache keyed by community_id, maps each Discord guild to its community, and subscribes to Realtime so a Save in Customize replaces that community's cached config within seconds. Every command then reads settings through its own guild — there is no global config and no fallback to another community's values: a community that hasn't saved anything gets a blank {}, and the code treats unset values as "not configured" instead of inventing defaults. Call loadCommunities() again from your guildCreate handler so a newly registered community is picked up without a restart. Prefer a file for one community? Download config.json in Customize exports the selected community's config only.

// ===== settings.js — per-community settings for the Civix bot =====
// Requires the supabase client from step 4 (service_role, laptop only).
const settingsByCommunity = new Map(); // community_id -> that community's config ONLY
const communityByGuild = new Map();    // discord guild_id -> community_id

async function loadCommunities() {
  const { data, error } = await supabase.from('communities').select('id, guild_id');
  if (error) { console.error('Civix: could not load communities', error.message); return; }
  communityByGuild.clear();
  (data || []).forEach(c => { if (c.guild_id) communityByGuild.set(String(c.guild_id), c.id); });
}

async function loadAllSettings() {
  const { data, error } = await supabase.from('bot_settings').select('community_id, config');
  if (error) { console.error('Civix: could not load settings', error.message); return; }
  settingsByCommunity.clear();
  (data || []).forEach(r => settingsByCommunity.set(r.community_id, r.config || {}));
  console.log('Civix: settings loaded for', settingsByCommunity.size, 'communities');
}

// The ONLY way bot code reads settings: by guild, resolved to its own
// community. Returns {} (blank) when that community has saved nothing —
// never another community's config, never built-in defaults.
function settingsForGuild(guildId) {
  const cid = communityByGuild.get(String(guildId));
  return cid ? (settingsByCommunity.get(cid) ?? {}) : {};
}
function communityIdForGuild(guildId) {
  return communityByGuild.get(String(guildId)) ?? null;
}
function featureOn(guildId, key) {
  return settingsForGuild(guildId).features?.[key] === true;
}

// Live updates: a Save in Customize replaces ONLY that community's entry.
function subscribeSettings() {
  supabase.channel('civix-bot-settings')
    .on('postgres_changes',
      { event: '*', schema: 'public', table: 'bot_settings' },
      (payload) => {
        if (payload.eventType === 'DELETE') {
          settingsByCommunity.delete(payload.old.community_id);
          return;
        }
        const row = payload.new;
        if (row && row.community_id) {
          settingsByCommunity.set(row.community_id, row.config || {});
          console.log('Civix: settings updated live for community', row.community_id);
        }
      })
    .subscribe();
}

// Startup (in your ready handler, after the Discord client logs in):
//   await loadCommunities();
//   await loadAllSettings();
//   subscribeSettings();
// And in your guildCreate handler: await loadCommunities();

// ===== Applying a community's settings inside a command =====
// Everything comes from THIS guild's config — currency name, panel
// channel, feature switches. Unset means "not configured here", so the
// feature stays off/quiet in this community instead of borrowing
// values from Civix defaults or another community.
async function handlePanel911(interaction) {
  const cfg = settingsForGuild(interaction.guildId);
  if (!featureOn(interaction.guildId, 'panel911')) {
    return interaction.reply({ content: 'The 911 panel is not enabled in this community.', ephemeral: true });
  }
  const channelName = cfg.panels?.p911?.channel; // blank until THIS community sets it
  if (!channelName) {
    return interaction.reply({ content: 'The 911 panel has no channel set in this community yet — an admin can set one in Customize.', ephemeral: true });
  }
  const channel = interaction.guild.channels.cache.find(c => c.name === channelName);
  // ...post the panel embed (title: cfg.panels.p911.title) to that channel
}

// Economy example: balances are per community AND per user, and the
// starting balance / currency name are this community's own values.
async function getBalance(guildId, userId) {
  const communityId = communityIdForGuild(guildId);
  if (!communityId) return null; // guild has no Civix community
  const cfg = settingsForGuild(guildId);
  const { data } = await supabase.from('wallets')
    .select('balance').eq('community_id', communityId).eq('user_id', userId)
    .maybeSingle();
  if (data) return data.balance;
  const start = cfg.economy?.startingBalance; // null until the community sets one
  if (start == null) return 0; // no starting balance configured in this community
  await supabase.from('wallets').insert({ community_id: communityId, user_id: userId, balance: start });
  return start;
}

How this answers the per-community requirement: settings are stored, loaded, cached, subscribed to and read per community end to end — the cache key is community_id, commands resolve their guild to exactly one community, a Realtime event for community A can only replace community A's entry, and a blank config stays blank in the bot (features off, no channel routing, no starting balance) until that community's owner saves their own values on this site.

Who can do what in this community's CAD

Being a member is not enough to change records. For each access role, switch on exactly which CAD actions that role may use in this community — view, create, edit and delete are separate rights. Everything starts off: until you grant a right here, that role can't do it. With Supabase connected these switches save into this community's config (permissions.cad) and the database policies in Setup step 1 (cad_allowed()) enforce them on every query — the toggles here and the rules in the database are the same settings.

Access roles are system levels, not your org chart. Owner / admin / officer / dispatch / civilian only control access to data. Your community's own department names, ranks and job titles are yours to invent — they live in Jobs & departments and Civilian records, and they never gate database access.
